title: NY State Assembly · District 28
area: Central Queens, including Forest Hills, Rego Park and Kew Gardens.

context.text: Incumbent Andrew Hevesi defeated Jonathan Rinaldi 87.7%-11.8% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Rinaldi remains on the November general-election ballot on the minor No Kings Party line; David Kemp, who withdrew from the Republican primary, is on the ballot on the 4 Our Immigrants Party line. The Working Families Party primary was canceled after Hevesi withdrew from that line.

On June 24, 2026, Rinaldi was arrested and arraigned on nearly 20 counts of fraud related to his 2025 New York City Council campaign, in which prosecutors say he used AI-generated content, including fabricated endorsements and deepfake videos of opponents.

summary.text: Andrew Hevesi is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Assembly District 28. He chairs the Children and Families Committee and also serves on the Codes, Health, Labor and Rules committees. He won the June 2026 Democratic primary against Jonathan Rinaldi with 87.7% of the vote.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in political science from Queens College.
Served as Chief of Staff for former New York State Assembly Member Jeff Klein.
Worked as Director of Community Affairs for the New York City Public Advocate before being elected to the Assembly.
Chairs the Children and Families Committee, a post he has held since at least the 2023-2024 session.

priorities.text: Child care affordability and workforce support, sponsoring a statewide child care workforce pay-equity fund and a tax credit expanding employer-provided dependent-care benefits.
Child welfare system funding, including raising the state reimbursement rate for preventive child protective services and adjusting foster-care payment rates for cost of living.
Domestic violence protections, sponsoring a bill to create a new state crime of "coercive control" against a family or household member.

positions.summary: Sponsored multiple bills to fund child care affordability and pay equity for the child care workforce, including a permanent child care workforce pay-equity fund and expanded dependent-care tax credits for working families.

record.text: Sponsored A63-A, establishing a child and family well-being program and fund to distribute grants to nonprofit community-based providers; referred to the Children and Families Committee as of January 2026.
Sponsored A492-A, establishing the permanent child care workforce pay equity fund; referred to the Children and Families Committee.
Sponsored A598, expanding the employer-provided child care tax credit to cover in-home and backup dependent care; referred to the Ways and Means Committee.
Sponsored A679, creating the crime of "coercive control" against a family or household member as a class E felony; referred to the Codes Committee.
Sponsored A487, raising the state reimbursement rate for preventive child protective services from 65% to 75%; reported and referred to the Ways and Means Committee.

summary.text: David Kemp is running on the 4 Our Immigrants Party line for NY State Assembly District 28. He withdrew from the Republican primary for the seat.

candidates.name: Jonathan Rinaldi
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to Andrew Hevesi (11.8% of the vote); remains on the general-election ballot on the No Kings Party line.

summary.text: Jonathan Rinaldi is a perennial Queens candidate running on the No Kings Party line for NY State Assembly District 28 after losing the Democratic primary to incumbent Andrew Hevesi. He was arrested in June 2026 on fraud charges related to his 2025 City Council campaign.

background.text: Born in New York; has worked as a consultant.
Previously ran for New York City Council District 28/29-area seats and for U.S. House in 2024, among other campaigns.

record.text: Arrested and arraigned on June 24, 2026 on nearly 20 counts of fraud tied to his 2025 New York City Council campaign against Lynn Schulman; prosecutors say he used AI-generated content, including fabricated endorsements attributed to public figures and fake news articles mimicking real outlets. The Queens Daily Eagle reported he also used AI-generated deepfake videos and images during both the 2025 City Council campaign and his 2026 Assembly primary campaign, though he was charged only over the 2025 campaign. He faces up to two years in prison if convicted.
